subject: Operator egress proof & containment — clarification Q&A
messages:
From: Alex Green <alex.green@ironcladhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: security@ironcladhealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operator egress proof and containment — RFP clarifications

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the initial RFP materials — the team is reviewing and we had a couple of follow-ups specifically around operator/data plane egress and containment guarantees. These details will feed into our control mapping and the SOC evidence packet. A few things we need clarified: 

1) Operator telemetry & control plane egress: can you provide a call flow showing which Redwood-managed services make outbound connections (FQDNs/IP ranges) and whether those calls are TLS-mutual-auth or one-way TLS? We need a short list we can map to our allowlist.

2) Sidecar/agent behavior: under a sidecar failure (OOM, restart, or network blackhole), does inference traffic fail-open to the host network or is it queued/rejected? Please describe the default behavior and any operator-configurable modes.

3) Tenant egress containment examples: can you provide two short adversary scenarios (one benign misconfiguration, one active exfiltration attempt) with the controls that would detect/block egress? 

If possible, attach a diagram that highlights operator vs tenant-controlled egress paths and any bastion/break-glass hops.

We'd appreciate a single consolidated note (and any artifacts) by EOD tomorrow so our security reviewers can proceed. Happy to schedule a 30m call if that's easier.

Thanks —
Alex Green
Senior Security Engineer
Ironclad Health
alex.green@ironcladhealth.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operator egress proof and containment — RFP clarifications

Alex — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; attaching a concise evidence packet and a topology snapshot that highlights the control plane vs tenant-data paths. I copied Kim and Ben — they'll add the traffic matrix and the failover behavior details.

1) Operator telemetry & control plane egress
- Outbound hosts: our control plane uses fixed egress ranges per region (US: 34.210.0.0/16, 34.211.0.0/16 — see attached topology snapshot). We also publish FQDNs (control.redwood-inference.com and telemetry.redwood-inference.com).
- Auth: control plane calls from the runtime are mutual-TLS (mTLS) by default for operator-managed connections. Telemetry uses mTLS for customer-assigned regions; in self-managed/private installs customers may optionally route telemetry to their collector.

2) Sidecar/agent behavior (default + modes)
- Default: sidecars are configured to fail-closed for egress to external operator endpoints. If the sidecar loses connectivity to the local inference runtime, requests are rejected with a clear 503; the host does not silently route inference traffic to public network.
- Operator-configurable modes: we offer a relaxed mode for lab/test clusters where the sidecar will queue for up to 30s and then fail-open if configured (not recommended for production). These modes are documented and gated by tenant policy flags in the console.

3) Tenant egress containment — two scenarios (summary)
- Misconfiguration: a mistaken allowlist entry opens a CIDR. Detection: TLS certificate anomaly detection + egress flow logs (7d by default) produce an alert; automatic circuit-breaker disables external egress until operator review.
- Active exfiltration: adversary attempts to stage bulk uploads to an external S3 endpoint. Detection/mitigation: content-layer egress DLP hooks (hash-based sampling), rate-limit enforcement per tenant, and fallback to isolation-mode where tenant traffic is routed to a quarantine VPC.

Attachments included: network-diagram-v2.png, segmentation-evidence.zip, redwood-topology-snapshot.pdf
Drive link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2B3Ctopology
Jira: JIRA-SEC-4321 (we'll add the traffic matrix card)

If that looks good, Kim/Ben will send the traffic/port matrix and a short write-up on operator-run bastion flows in the next message. Happy to hop on a call tomorrow at 11am PT — let me know.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Architect, Security
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-topology-snapshot.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

Olga — this is great, thanks. Couple quick clarifications before we mark the item closed:

- The CIDR ranges you listed for US control plane (34.210.0.0/16, 34.211.0.0/16) — are those the only ranges in use for the control plane in us-west and us-east? We need explicit per-region ranges.

If you can include the per-region CIDR table and an example response body (including trace-id field name and sample value), that will satisfy our reviewers.

I can take a 30m call tomorrow if helpful — available 12–2pm ET.

Olga / Ben — forwarding the traffic matrix excerpt and sample runtime response. I'll attach the full CSV to the evidence bundle after review.

Traffic matrix excerpt (ports and endpoints):
- control.redwood-inference.com:443 (mTLS) -> 34.210.12.45 (us-east-1 control lane)
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com:443 (mTLS) -> 34.211.33.22 (us-west-2 telemetry lane)
- metrics.push.redwood-inference.com:443 (one-way TLS) -> 52.23.11.8 (metrics collector)

Sidecar failure sample response (JSON):
{ "status": 503, "error": "inference_unavailable", "trace_id": "trc-8f3b2a9d" }

Notes: default behavior is to return 503 + trace_id; all trace_ids map to the tenant's request id and are surfaced in the operator console for triage. The relaxed queueing mode returns 202 + queued=true and a queue_id if configured.

I've attached segmentation-evidence.zip containing per-region CIDR tables (csv) and the full traffic matrix. We'll also add the per-region CIDR list to the Drive link Olga shared.

Kimberly Park
Principal Network Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
